messages:
emily (docs): Heads-up — opened a docs PR with a compact playbook for tuning batching/caching/quantization. Includes migration tips and SDK snippet updates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 :wave:

matt (optimize): nice. can you call out recommended batch_size windows per model family? folks keep asking about llama2 vs mixtral.

emily (docs): added a table but keeping it small. currently: small models: 32-64, mid: 8-32, large: 1-8. noted caveat about sequence length.

raj (eng-ml): quick note — those ranges are ok but we should add guidance about kv-cache warmup and prefix caching for chat workloads. otherwise perf regresses on long convo sessions.

emily (docs): good catch. i'll add a short example showing prefix cache usage + expected latency delta.

alex (sdk): spotted two broken snippets in the python SDK example. the streaming snippet uses the old client API (`client.generate_stream`). changed one line locally, running tests. Proposed replacement: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
for chunk in client.generate(model="rwd-mixtral-8x", input="...", stream=True):
    print(chunk.text, end="")
```

jen (devex): please also add a JS equivalent. a lot of customers copy-paste from the JS SDK. keep it minimal, show stream + reconnect fallback.

matt (optimize): also add a short blurb about quant profiles: what they mean (int8 vs nf4-ish), when to pick conservative vs aggressive, and a 'regression watchlist' (bleu/accuracy drop quick test).

emily (docs): yep — i made a separate section: "Quant profiles & when to use them" with bullet points and an example quant_profile JSON.

alex (sdk): pushed a tiny commit to the PR that updates the Python snippet and the JS stub (see commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/1a2b3c4). CI flagged a lint warning for code-block formatting; i'll fix in a followup.

docs-bot: PR 482: title changed to "Tuning playbook: batching, caching, quant profiles (compact)" — reviewers requested: @matt (optimize), @alex (sdk) — checks: link-check failed (1 broken link)

emily (docs): ack. looking for the broken link now — i think it's the internal design reference to the batching scheduler that moved.

matt (optimize): that internal link should be `/eng-runtime/batching-scheduler.md` — we moved it under eng-runtime last month. update to absolute path or remove.

emily (docs): fixed link to /eng-runtime/batching-scheduler.md and pushed. also added the kv-cache example Raj asked for.

raj (eng-ml): quick perf note to include: with prefix caching, effective tokens/sec can be ~2-3x for repeated context patterns on smaller batches. adding a tiny bench snippet would help users set expectations.

emily (docs): i added a bench snippet (curl + micro-bench) and a sentence: "expect 1.5–3x throughput improvements for repeated-prefix chat patterns depending on model and hardware."

jen (devex): one more ask: can we include a short migration checklist for customers migrating from hosted->dedicated? they often forget to pin quant_profile and it causes flicker.

emily (docs): added a checklist item: "pin quant_profile and model version; validate with seeded prompts; enable canary rollout" — also linked to the rollout doc.

alex (sdk): FYI the JS reconnect fallback snippet i added uses the new `onReconnect` hook in the SDK; verified locally. please call out minimum SDK versions in the note.

emily (docs): added note: "requires SDK >= 0.9.3 (JS) / 1.2.0 (Python)" near snippets.

matt (optimize): looks good to me. last QA: can we add a one-line note on cost tradeoffs when using aggressive quant (e.g., save ~30–60% GPU memory but watch for small LM quality regressions)?

emily (docs): done — short paragraph with suggested quick AB test prompt set.

docs-bot: PR 482: all checks passing ✅ — reviewers: matt, alex — merge queued.

emily (docs): merging after one more thumbs-up. thanks everyone :heart:

raj (eng-ml): thumbs up — maybe add perf numbers to the example later when we have mixtral bench runs.

emily (docs): noted — i'll file a follow-up issue to attach micro-bench CSVs once we finish the perf run. issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/129

alex (sdk): great. will follow up on lint fix and the JS fallback tests.

emily (docs): closing thread once merged. thanks for the quick reviews! :tada:
